Refuse to fill any line you cannot cite.
_strings.@@57b5120e87da: Treaty conformity — VT conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from VT income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the VT return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Vermont's resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income and does NOT add back federally treaty-exempt income; it explicitly SUBTRACTS it. Form IN-111 Line 1 is "Federal Adjusted Gross Income — Enter the amount from your federal Form 1040." The DOR "Resident" page states: "If you are a Vermont resident, your income starts with federal adjusted gross income minus the following: Income exempted from state taxation by the laws of the United States..." Line 2 (Net Modifications to Federal AGI, via Schedule IN-112) contains the standard state additions/subtractions with no treaty-income add-back. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is additionally listed as a Vermont subtraction (not an addition), it is not re-taxed -> conforms = true.
_strings.@@69ffd69498ad: Vermont Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — Full-year and part-year Vermont residents who qualify for and receive the federal Earned Income Tax Credit. As of 2023 it is available to all qualifying VT residents regardless of whether they, their spouse, or qualifying dependents have an SSN or ITIN (such returns must be paper-filed).

Not independently confirmed (verify the figure): Renter Credit (renter rebate / circuit-breaker).
_strings.@@9595d2e5f0a2: Renter Credit (renter rebate / circuit-breaker) — Vermont renters who, for 2023: (1) were domiciled in Vermont as their main home for the entire calendar year, (2) paid rent for at least six months in Vermont (need not be consecutive), (3) are not claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's return, and (4) have income at or below the Renter Credit income limits, which vary by county of residence and number of household members.
_strings.@@b187e86039d2: 2023 Vermont Income Tax Return Booklet / Form IN-111 Instructions (Rev. 10/23), Vermont Dept. of Taxes — p.7 (Line 4 '2023 Vermont Standard Deduction' chart incl. $1,150-per-box additional deduction; Line 5e 'Multiply Line 5d by $4,850' personal exemption; Line 7 Vermont Taxable Income; Line 8 Vermont Income Tax incl. 3%-of-AGI minimum for federal AGI over $150,000) and p.12 '2023 Vermont Tax Rate Schedules' (Schedules X, Y-1, Y-2, Z; also published standalone at https://tax.vermont.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/RateSched-2023.pdf p.1); pp.13-17 '2023 Vermont Tax Tables'. Available to all qualifying VT residents regardless of SSN/ITIN status of taxpayer, spouse, or dependents.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form IN-111, Line 8: "Vermont Income Tax from tax table or tax rate schedule (If Line 1 is greater than $150,000, see instructions)". Line 7: "Vermont Taxable Income (SUBTRACT Line 6 from Line 3. If less than zero, enter -0-)", where Line 6 = Line 4 standard deduction + Line 5e personal exemption deduction. Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,150 — Line 4 instructions (p.7): 'You also receive an additional deduction of $1,150 for each standard deduction box checked on the federal Form 1040' (born before Jan. 2, 1959). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — use the Line 4 chart (e.g., Single 1 box $8,150, 2 boxes $9,300; MFJ/QW up to 4 boxes $18,650; MFS up to 4 boxes $11,600; HoH up to 2 boxes $12,850).); blind ($1,150 — Same $1,150-per-checked-box additional standard deduction applies to blindness boxes on federal Form 1040 (Line 4 chart, p.7). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it via the form's Line 4 chart.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form IN-111, Line 3 "Federal AGI with Modifications" = Line 1 federal AGI (federal Form 1040, Line 11) plus/minus Line 2 net modifications to federal AGI (Schedule IN-112, Part I, Line 18). With no Vermont modifications, Line 3 equals federal AGI, so plain federal AGI is the correct input for most filers. The op then subtracts the shipped Vermont standard deduction (IN-111 Line 4) and $4,850 per exemption (Lines 5a-5e) to reproduce Line 7, Vermont Taxable Income. Tax-table mandate below $75,000: each 2023 Vermont Tax Rate Schedule prints 'TAXABLE INCOME UNDER $75,000 USE THE TAX TABLES' across its sub-$75,000 rows. The 2023 Vermont Tax Tables (IN-111 Instr. pp.13-17) compute tax at the midpoint of each $100 band, rounded to whole dollars (spot-verified: Single $30,000-$30,100 band = $1,007 vs $1,005 exact bracket math at $30,000; $74,900-$75,000 band matches midpoint math for all four statuses), so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table below $75,000. CRITICAL - 3% minimum tax not modeled: IN-111 Instr. p.7, Line 8: 'Taxpayers who have a federal Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) greater than $150,000 must pay a minimum Vermont tax of 3% of federal AGI. If your federal AGI, Line 1, is greater than $150,000, enter the amount that is higher: 1) 3% of your federal AGI less interest from U.S. obligations, or 2) tax calculated on Vermont Taxable Income, Line 7, using the applicable tax rate schedule.' This op computes only (2); when the 3% floor binds (typically large modifications/deductions relative to AGI), plain bracket math understates Line 8. Printed base-tax constants are rounded: the schedules' 'VT Base Tax' dollar constants are rounded to whole dollars and differ from the exact cumulative bracket sums by up to $0.50 (e.g., Single $1,521.00 printed vs $1,520.90 exact; MFS $4,820.00 printed vs $4,819.64 exact; HoH $2,038.00 printed vs $2,038.48 exact). Form arithmetic using the printed constants can therefore differ by $1 from this op's exact marginal-bracket math. The printed schedules break a row at exactly $75,000 solely to flag the tax-table mandate — the rate does NOT change at $75,000 (e.g., MFJ 3.35% actually runs $0-$75,850; Single 6.60% runs $45,400-$110,050). Same-rate rows are merged in the shipped brackets; the math is identical. Qualifying Widow(er)/surviving spouse: Schedule Y-1 is captioned 'Married Filing Jointly; Qualifying Widow(er); or Civil Union Filing Jointly' and the QW standard deduction is the same $14,050, so the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping matches Vermont exactly. Civil Union Filing Separately uses Schedule Y-2 (married_filing_separately); Civil Union Filing Jointly uses Y-1. Additional standard deduction not applied by the engine: $1,150 per standard-deduction box checked on federal Form 1040 (born before Jan. 2, 1959, or blind) is added to the Line 4 standard deduction per the chart on IN-111 Instr. p.7 — compute those cases from the form's chart. Exemption gates not modeled: Line 5a counts yourself ONLY if no one can claim you as a dependent on a 2023 return; Line 5b (spouse/CU partner) must be left blank if filing status is Qualifying Widow(er) or Married Filing Separately. Vermont has no itemized-deduction option on the 2023 IN-111 — Line 4 offers only the Vermont standard deduction (there is no itemized line on the form). Steps between Line 8 and the final Line 14 'Vermont Income Tax' are NOT modeled: Line 9 Net Adjustment to Vermont Tax (Schedule IN-119 Part I — additions such as recapture of a Vermont tax credit and 24% of certain additional federal taxes on IRA/HSA/MSA distributions, federal ITC recapture, Form 4972 lump-sum distributions; subtractions such as the credit for the elderly or disabled, Vermont-based ITC, farm income averaging credit), and Lines 11-13 Vermont Charitable Contribution Deduction — despite the line caption, the instructions describe it as a nonrefundable tax CREDIT equal to 5% of the first $20,000 of eligible charitable contributions (max $1,000, Line 13) subtracted from tax on Line 14, not an income deduction. Part-year residents and nonresidents: Line 15 income adjustment percentage (Schedule IN-113, Line 35) multiplies Line 14 to get Line 16 Adjusted Vermont Income Tax — not modeled; full-year residents use 100%.
